reasons: Cited text supports the compliant call: 19.1 gives a professional/workmanlike standard plus material conformity to documentation and specifications; 19.2 gives a 90-day Deliverable warranty (from the later of delivery or acceptance) and continuous conformity for Hosted Services throughout the subscription term, meeting or exceeding both the 90-day services and 12-month software benchmarks.

Remedy stack in 19.4 (re-perform, repair or replace at no charge, with termination and refund of Fees as backstop, expressly non-exclusive for fraud, IP, confidentiality, privacy, security and indemnified claims) satisfies the preferred repair/replace/refund requirement.

19.5 disclaims only implied warranties and expressly states no disclaimer limits an express warranty, service level, indemnity or remedy, so the disclaimer does not swallow the express warranty; 19.3 covers Applicable Law compliance and malicious code.
The failed deterministic period check is a defensible false negative: the period is spelled out as "ninety days" rather than in numerals, and the rationale correctly identifies and explains this.

No redline or counterparty comment is proposed, which is the correct output for a compliant finding; minor residual softeners (malicious code limited to code "intentionally introduced by Vendor"; "Fees" defined narrowly as the Implementation Fee) are not material enough to convert this into an actionable deviation.
